## 2. Print stream and bar kernel: vol_1700 on _CANC prints
Code: code/th_bars/kernels.py:10-33 `k_cum` mode 0, built at code/th_bars/build_month.py:91-93 (threshold = N x s_vol); print rule D8_PRINT_RULE.md sections 1 and 4.
1. Record side and run merge: exactly as D8_NYAM_SPEC_B7bfd33b7.md section 2 steps 1-2 (quote-rule side from bid/ask at the trade, buy test first; consecutive records with equal price and equal side merge into one print, no time condition, not across the 09:30 / 12:00 ET session boundaries; the print is stamped with the timestamp of the next different print, last print of the session: its last record). td 20261110 NY AM: 234,912 records -> 208,040 prints; 1027: 169,694 -> 138,622.
2. Threshold thr = 1700 x s_vol contracts (float, fixed per trading date; s_vol from the table below): 1771.424 (td 20261027), 1888.743 (td 20261110). Bar: opens at the first print of the session (o = its price); each print adds its (merged) size to the bar volume and to the cumulative metric; the bar closes at the first print where cumulative volume >= thr (>=); the closing print stays WHOLE in the closing bar (no split, no carry; overshoot stays in the bar); next bar starts at 0 at the next print (kernels.py:21-31). h/l = extremes of print prices, c = closing print price, n = prints in the bar. Known time = stamp of the closing print. The open remainder at session end is emitted with part = 1 and never signals but stays in the series (its close is the `previous close` of the next session's first bar).
3. VERIFIED: rebuilt from tape for both days: 130 / 155 bars, all columns equal the stored CANC bars (bars of 1110: first bar volume 1,889 contracts, known 14:30:09.524Z).
**Day scales (how the per-day constant is built; identical code for every book of this page).** code/th_bars/build_month.py:13-32 `scales()`: for each trading date (td = ET + 6 h) the stats row of the 20 stats rows BEFORE that td (the current day is never used; values <= 0 dropped; at least 5 values, else the first-60-day median) are medianed; scale = that median / (median of the first 60 days). Columns: `rng` = daily range in points, built per UTC trade file, max over the pieces, / 4 (code/th_bars/stats.py:18; the quirk and the A/B holes are written out in autopilot/D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md section 2); `vol` = contracts of every record of the td; `n` = number of PRINTS of the td (run merge, same price and same tape side, never across a session code), table /mnt/l2/l2vast/_d8spec/runstats/stats_day.parquet. Checked here: for td 20261110 the runstats `n` = 463,946 = my own run count of the store tape (same price + same store side, break at session-code change): equal; the `_bars` stats_day.parquet holds the record count 530,480 instead (different column), so a coder must use the merged-print count for dib / tick rows.
**Data end / holes (read first).** The engine's stats tables end at td 20261113 and have no row for 20261102, 20261103, 20261104 (and 20261105 is a half day; autopilot/D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md header). The engine trade store also lacks the days 20261102-20261104 (trade files present: 1026-1030, 1105, 1106, 1108, 1109, 1110..1113). Column A = the engine as stored (what the stored bars and events used); column B (rng-based constants only) = the same function on a table with the holes filled and 1116-1120 added from hist_replica (a FORMULA result from D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md section 2, not an engine run). Which of A or B NT8 should copy for tomorrow is NOT decided here (lead).

## 3. Trigger: trig_structure_level, variant sopen_cross, buf 0.0 (exact rule)
Code: code/th_grid/triggers_b/impl_st.py:192-197 `_break_cross`, :214-216 (session open level), :219-241 `level_sig` (sopen branch at :235-238), registry.py:39 (variant `sopen_cross` = kind `sopen`, mode `cross`).
1. Series: one continuous series of all stored vol_1700 CANC bars (all sessions since 2023-04, sorted by known time, including part = 1 remainder bars). Session = sess_id = td x 10 + code (code 0 Asia 18:00-02:00, 1 London 02:00-08:30, 2 pre 08:30-09:30, 3 NY AM 09:30-12:00, 4 NY PM 12:00-16:00, 5 16:00-18:00 ET).
2. Level `so_j` = the OPEN of the first bar of bar j's own session (impl_st.py:214-216: `so` = o at the first bar of each sess_id, forward-filled); i.e. the first PRINT price of the session (first merged run of the session; for NY AM the price of the first record at/after 09:30:00 ET). Points, no buffer: `buf` = 0.0, `thr_j = so_j + 0.0 x ATR14` (the ATR term is multiplied by 0; it only matters if ATR were NaN, i.e. at the very start of the series).
3. Edge test (`_break_cross`, :192-197): up_j = close_j > thr_j AND NOT (close_{j-1} > thr_{j-1}), where thr_{j-1} is the level of the PREVIOUS BAR OF THE SERIES with ITS OWN session's open. LONG = up_j. down_j = close_j < thr_j AND NOT (close_{j-1} < thr_{j-1}) -> SHORT (only if not long). Strict inequalities. For the FIRST bar of NY AM (j-1 = last bar of the 08:30-09:30 session, thr_{j-1} = that session's open) the previous-bar test uses the 08:30 session's open: this is how the engine behaves and 460 of 6,202 signals in the history are first-bar signals (td 20261110: the very first signal, bar known 14:30:09.524Z, close 27745.50 > open 27743.00, LONG). The NT8 strategy must therefore keep the 08:30-09:30 vol_1700 bars (CANC prints, same threshold) too, including their open level and last close.
4. No other filter; the signal is on the closing print of the bar; fires at most once per bar; no unit; no other market. Not verified: behaviour at a contract roll (the engine back-adjusts bar prices at rolls from the bar iid in triggers_b, my numpy version without any adjustment gives the same 6,201 events across all contract rolls inside the 3-year history, so the adjustment does not change this rule).
VERIFIED: (a) engine module = events 6,201 / 6,201 (ts, side); (b) my numpy implementation of 2-3 = the same 6,201 (+1 session-end-second event the engine drops); (c) the INPUTS table below (computed by me from the stored CANC bars) gives 13 (1027) and 12 (1110) signals = the engine's.

## 4. Bracket S8U, sides, window, one position (unit rule spelled out)
- S8U = symmetric: stop = target = clip(8 x u, 10, 120) points (code/th_brkt/brkt_build.py:17, cl at the clip line), 1 lot, fixed from the entry fill.
- How the engine's `u` was made for THIS book (found by recomputation): events come from the CANC bars, then build_from_file (brkt_build.py:88-98) takes u from the OLD vol_1700 bars (/mnt/l2/l2vast/_bars/vol_1700, unmerged raw records) = rolling MEDIAN over 50 bars of (high - low) in points, window including the signal bar, min_periods 10, floor 0.25 (brkt_build.py:40), looked up with merge_asof at the event time: the nearest old-bar signal at or before the event ts within 120 s; if none (402 of 6,201 events) the median of ALL old-bar ranges is used (brkt_build.py:92-93). I reproduced the stops of the events file exactly this way (6,201 of 6,201).
- If NT8 instead computes u from its own CANC vol_1700 chart bars (rolling-50 median of range including the signal bar), 4,898 of 6,201 stops (78.99%) equal the engine's; the others differ (median absolute difference 0). All events of 2026-04 to 2026-11 have stop = target = 120.0 (share 100% each month), including all sample-day events (columns below), because the median bar range is ~28 pt (8u = 224 >> 120); 8u falls below 120 only when u < 15 pt. Practical reading: fixed 120/120 reproduces the engine in the live period; the lead decides rule versus fixed (NOT decided here).
- Sides: both. Window: NY AM bars code 3, part 0, scheduled exit 12:00 ET + 1 s.
**Signal to engine event (VERIFIED in code).** Event time `ts` = floor(known time of the signal bar to whole seconds) + 2 s (code/th_nyeng/ny_build.py:32; code/th_brkt/brkt_build.py:42); events with ts >= the session-end instant are dropped (ny_build.py:33, brkt_build.py:46); session-end instant = the next ET session boundary after the signal bar (code/th_swap/common.py:32-40; for NY AM = 12:00 ET); the exit cap (N = 120 s, code/th_fakefill/cap_exit.py:9,20) is applied to the event file. Only bars with session code 3 (ET 09:30-12:00; code/th_swap/common.py:41-44) and `part` = 0 (not the truncated last bar of a session) can signal (ny_build.py:29; brkt_build.py:38-39). Sample-day checks: my re-run of the engine module on the stored bars gives the engine events file exactly for both sample days (counts below) and over the whole history (counts below).
**One-position / fill / exits (SPEC text copied from autopilot/D8_BUILD_SPEC.md block (b2), simulator code/replica/sim.py: NOT re-verified here).** MARKET order sent at event time; filled 1.0 s later (LAT_FILL) walking the 10-level book (buy at the ask side, sell at the bid side); stop = stop order at fill -/+ stop_pts (triggered by a print at/through the level, then market order walking the book), target = resting limit at fill +/- tgt_pts; ONE position per book: an event while the book is in a trade, an exit is pending or an entry is in flight is dropped (the next event after the exit is traded); scheduled session-end exit at 12:00 ET + 1.0 s (if no print follows within 120 s the exit is the last print before it); contract roll: flat 1 ns before the roll second, entries skipped roll-120 s to roll+300 s. Sizes: 1 lot per book in the engine runs (bare R0 base set; no stack rules in the TRADES blocks).

## Relay questions 2026-11-24 21:25Z (answers from engine code, read-only)
- Q1a CORRECTION: state is NOT reset at the session change for the previous-bar test. S (`so`) = open of the first bar of the bar's own session, forward-filled within that session (code/th_grid/triggers_b/impl_st.py:214-216); the edge test `_break_cross` (impl_st.py:192-197) uses `pc = np.r_[nan, c[:-1]]` and `pth = np.r_[nan, thr[:-1]]` over the ONE continuous series, so for the first bar of a session the previous bar is the last bar (incl. part = 1 remainder) of the previous session, compared with THAT session's S. Only the very first bar of the whole series has no previous bar. So LONG = close > S and NOT (previous series bar's close > previous series bar's S); on the first NY AM bar that previous S is the 08:30-09:30 session's S. Verified: 460 of 6,202 signals are first-bar signals and my numpy rule built this way reproduces all 6,201 events; td 20261110 first signal 14:30:09.524Z LONG.
- Q1b S is the first PRINT of the session (first bar open = first merged run's price = first record's price at/after 09:30:00 ET), NOT the open of a 1-minute bar: the row is vol_1700 event bars, the open is `o` of the first stored bar of the sess_id (td 20261110: 27743.00 = 110972 ticks). Short = mirrored with `<`; both strict.
